title: $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$ is flat over $E_X$
statement:
For a finite extension $E$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Qlb$ and every scheme $X$, the extension
of scalars $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}\otimes_{E_X}-\colon\Mod_{E_X}\to\Mod_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}}$ along
$E_X\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$ ([def-sfb-subfield-to-qlbar-coefficient-map],
[sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]) preserves finite limits; that is, $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$ is flat over
$E_X$.

proof.text: Put $R=E_X$, $B=\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$. Choose a small site skeleton and coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention]. The closed tensor and monoidal local equivalences are [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor, det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-local-iso]. Thus [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] identifies internal and sectionwise module tensors. The underlying extension of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] is this tensor, with $B$ acting on its first factor.

source.place: Module conventions in returned step 1; the existing tensor comparison replaces its inline argument

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-qlbar-tail-module-colimit], the nonempty directed poset $I_E$ of finite $F\supseteq E$ gives $B=\operatorname{colim}_{F\in I_E}F_X$ in $R$-module sheaves, with the specified coefficient-inclusion legs.

source.place: First sentence; extracted cofinal coefficient module-colimit argument

proof.text: Set $T_F=\operatorname{Res}_{R\to F_X}(F_X\otimes_R-)$ and $T=\operatorname{Res}_{R\to B}(B\otimes_R-)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits] and tensor symmetry [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], step 2 gives $\theta_M:\operatorname{colim}_F T_F(M)\cong T(M)$. Its $F$-leg is $s\otimes m\mapsto q_F(s)\otimes m$. This commutes with $m\mapsto u(m)$ and coefficient inclusions, so $\theta$ identifies the natural transformations on every arrow $u$.

source.place: Tensor-colimit sentence; returned step 4, retaining the canonical maps

proof.text: Each $T_F$ preserves kernels: apply [lem-sfb-subfield-flat] and the limit-preserving restriction of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. The fixed category $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], so its filtered colimit functor preserves finite limits. Now [lem-sfb-arrow-exact-colimits] identifies the colimit of these kernel cones with the kernel cone of the colimit arrow. Step 3 therefore identifies $T(\ker u)\to T(M)$ with the kernel of $T(u)$, for every $u:M\to N$.

source.place: Last sentence; returned steps 5-6 now use the existing Grothendieck and arrow-kernel lemmas

proof.text: The balanced tensor formula $b\otimes(u+v)(m)=b\otimes u(m)+b\otimes v(m)$ proves that $T$ is additive [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Since it preserves kernels, [lem-sfb-kernel-cokernel-finite-exactness] implies that $T$ preserves finite limits, including the empty limit.

source.place: Last sentence; the existing kernel criterion replaces the finite-diagram calculation

proof.text: For a finite diagram $D$, the extension comparison $a:B\otimes_R\lim D\to\lim(B\otimes_R D)$ is $B$-linear. Sectionwise limits [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise] show that restriction makes it the invertible comparison of step 5. Its inverse is $B$-linear: $a(b a^{-1}y)=by=a(a^{-1}(by))$, and cancel $a$. Thus $a$ is an isomorphism of $B$-modules, proving the statement.

source.place: Last sentence; returned step 8, reflection of the specified finite-limit comparison

proof_origin.place: Finer repair of the filtered-colimit proof: cofinal coefficient module colimit extracted, existing tensor-comparison, Grothendieck, arrow-kernel and finite-exactness lemmas reused. All colimits remain in E_X-modules.
